project.name: Ouroboros V2 Selfhost Automation Pipeline
project.tagline: Hourly turn-based control plane for importer hardening, self-host pipeline progress, and stage-2 validation.
project.northStar: Get KAIN to a trustworthy self-hosted compiler path without destabilizing the currently used bootstrap corridor, then harden the importer and stage-2 flow until the language is strong enough to carry large systems like a 3D engine.
retirementCriteria: Produce a real self-hosted kain.exe from the bootstrapped/self-host pipeline.
Reach a practical 1:1 Rust -> KAIN -> compile path for the intended crates surface under crates/.
Include the hard self-host slices and codegen-heavy surfaces, including cli, kain-import, kain-sys-codegen, and UE5-facing/codegen-facing crate paths where applicable.
Keep the bootstrap corridor intact until the self-hosted path is trustworthy enough to replace it.
If phase 2 is materially complete, generate a concrete phase-3 plan instead of stopping at celebration.

priorities: Protect the live bootstrap corridor while expanding the self-host corridor.
Treat the Rust importer as the highest leverage frontier until strict self-host import is much cleaner.
Keep lane definitions, artifact expectations, and repair rules data-driven instead of scattering ad hoc command sequences.
Use OuroborosV2 for manifests, repair rules, probes, and artifact analysis; use Kain for real implementation changes.
Resolve roots from the current checkout or explicit environment overrides instead of hardcoded absolute paths.
Record exact evidence for every promotion claim so the next agent can continue instead of re-auditing.

importer: cargo check -p kain-import -p cli -p kain-selfhost -p kain-sys-codegen
pipeline: cargo run -p cli --bin kain -- selfhost phase1
validation: cargo run -p cli --bin kain -- selfhost phase2

importer.goal: Harden the Rust importer and strict self-host import lane so reflexive import is less fragile and more diagnosable.
focusAreas: RustTransformer gaps that block self-host import
battle-tested regression coverage for importer behavior
hardRules: Do not touch the bootstrap corridor unless the change directly removes a proved blocker and is documented.
Prefer importer correctness and diagnostics over speculative surface expansion.
If a new unsupported Rust shape is found, record the exact file, syntax shape, and failure mode.

pipeline.goal: Strengthen phase-1 and phase-2 orchestration so importer, bundle emission, round-trip, and stage-2 assembly remain reproducible.
hardRules: Keep pipeline behavior data-driven through inventories, manifests, and typed lane contracts.
Do not hide failures behind soft wording; route them into explicit artifact or report fields.
Avoid mixing repair-rule mutations into pure pipeline turns unless required for reproducibility.

repair.goal: Reduce the highest-value phase-2 blockers by improving repair rules, taxonomy, and targeted compile-safe transformations.
hardRules: Fix blocker families, not one-off log lines, whenever the pattern is real.
Keep repair scope narrow and explain why the rule is bootstrap-safe.
Do not promote a repair rule without concrete evidence from current outputs.

validation.goal: Prove current self-host progress with executable evidence and convert ambiguous failure states into crisp next actions.
hardRules: Prefer running the narrowest commands that answer the next question.
If a command is too heavy or unstable, use a fallback command and document the tradeoff.
Do not claim promotion unless the corresponding artifact or log exists.

docs.goal: Keep the control plane legible so future agents know where the real self-host logic lives and what changed last.
hardRules: Docs must point to live code, not just old plans.
Treat scattered docs as a consolidation problem, not a reason to write more drift.
Prefer concise operational notes over aspiration-only prose.

automationPrompt.name: Codex Hourly Selfhost Loop
instructions: Read automation/config/pipeline.config.json, automation/README.md, automation/BACKLOG.md, automation/docs/SELFHOST_LOGIC_MAP.md, and automation/docs/PIPELINE_BLUEPRINT.md first.
Determine the next turn by counting markdown files in automation/reports and adding one, or just run node automation/scripts/next-turn.mjs with no --turn argument.
Generate the brief with node automation/scripts/next-turn.mjs.
Execute exactly one lane-appropriate improvement for the active turn.
Treat ouroboros/ as the control plane and the repo root as the live implementation workspace.
Protect the bootstrap corridor unless the current turn has strong evidence for a safe targeted fix.
Prefer data-driven manifests, inventories, typed contracts, and repair rules over scattered hardcoded logic.
Validate with the lane commands from the config. If they are too expensive or unstable, use fallback commands and record why.
Write a report to automation/reports named TURN-XXX-<lane>.md using automation/templates/session-report.md.
Update automation/CHANGELOG.md with one concise entry for the turn so there is a unified history across the whole pipeline.
Record exact files touched, commands run, passes, failures, and the best next handoff for the following agent.
Treat the finish line as a real self-hosted kain.exe and a near-1:1 import/compile path across the intended Rust crate surface, not merely prettier reports.
If phase 2 appears complete, produce the next phase-3 plan instead of stopping.
